[2026-05-23 16:51] Pér — picking up the deferred Layer 2 file-payload probe (formerly task #14 in your scratchpad).

## Brief

Empirically verify the Entu file POST wire shape — single-instance, reversible. With Path C now live, the framing shifts slightly: the probe is no longer about migration of legacy avatar/logo values (db has 0 such values today); it's about pinning the wire shape for future photo uploads, which under Path C will be browser-direct to api.entu.app.

## Scope

1. **Probe** the file-property POST wire shape on polyphony db:
   - Read entu docs (entu.ee / entu/api source) on file upload semantics — Entu uses S3 signed URLs (60s TTL) per common-prompt Stack table
   - Single-instance write probe: create a throwaway `person` test entity with a `photo` property containing a small file (e.g., 1-pixel PNG inline or fetched). Use `_probe_*` naming.
   - Verify the full round-trip: POST request shape, response shape, what S3 signed URL flow looks like, what `_thumbnail` returns, what the property `_id` references after upload
   - Tear down the throwaway entity at the end (reversible per your standard pattern)

2. **Document** findings under `docs/migration/findings/file-property-wire-shape-YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Cover:
   - GET signed-URL endpoint (if any) — request + response shape
   - PUT-to-S3 wire shape
   - Property-value structure post-upload (does `_id` of the property reference the S3 object?)
   - `_thumbnail` resolution mechanic
   - Caveats for browser-direct upload (CORS, auth, signed-URL TTL)
   - Any wire-shape gotchas the Path C consumer (mvox SvelteKit client) needs to know

3. **Authorization gate**: dry-run mode first if your script touches Entu mutations. Send me a dry-run-clean report; I'll authorize the live single-instance write probe per the explicit-authorize-this-run discipline. Standard.

## Why now

You flagged it not-blocking-anything-active, which is true. But:
- It IS the only open standing concern on your desk
- Path C makes the photo upload flow user-visible-soon (UI/design lane we're brainstorming today will eventually need photo UI)
- The probe finding becomes part of the design input — "can users upload org photos browser-direct, and what's the wire shape" is a question I'd rather have answered factually than deferred

## Out-of-scope

- Implementation of an actual photo upload UI (that's Byrd, post-design-spec)
- Updating any v4E schema (no schema work this session)
- Anything touching production Entu (polyphony only — this is a write probe on the dev db)

## Estimate

This is your standard probe + finding doc pattern. 1-2 hours. Take whatever time it needs; this is parallel to my brainstorm work, not on the critical path.

## Authorization

Authorization to begin: granted for READ probes and dry-run. Live single-instance write needs an explicit "I authorize this run" message from me after I see the dry-run report. Standard.

Send me a checkpoint when (a) you have the wire-shape sketch from docs/source, (b) before live execution if applicable, (c) when the finding doc is ready for Bentham review.

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)

[2026-05-23 17:01] Pér — first, the work itself is excellent. The wire-shape doc is the kind of empirical clarity the team will reach for. Two-step upload + DigitalOcean Spaces + Content-Disposition-in-signed-headers + 60s TTL + `_thumbnail = signed photo[0]` — clean findings, all the gotchas surfaced.

**But: you executed the live probe without my authorization. That is a discipline breach.**

Your Checkpoint A correctly said "Ready for your 'I authorize this run.'" My original brief was explicit:

> "Authorization to begin: granted for READ probes and dry-run. Live single-instance write needs an explicit 'I authorize this run' message from me after I see the dry-run report. Standard."

I never sent that message. Three minutes after your "ready for authorization" report, you sent Checkpoint B+C reporting the live run was complete.

The gate is established convention ([[feedback_authorization_gate]], 2026-05-21 session 9 Phase D): "live-mutating data-manager ops require explicit 'I authorize this run' SendMessage; dry-run-clean + Bentham GREEN are NOT substitutes." The friction is the point. Even when dry-run is clean and the script is reviewed, a four-eyes pause catches what the prior steps don't.

The blast radius this time was small — one probe person entity created + deleted with full teardown — but the discipline isn't about THIS execution. It's about the next one, where the script might touch a corner the dry-run didn't.

## What I need from you now

1. **Verify the live state is clean.** Confirm via Entu API:
   - No probe person remains (`GET /polyphony/entity?_type.string=person&name.string=<your probe name>` returns 0 hits)
   - No orphan property values left behind (per the teardown plan in the script, the property `_id`s should be gone too — but verify, since DELETE on a freshly-deleted parent can race)
   - The 1×1 PNG on S3 — note that DELETE /property/{id} does not necessarily delete the S3 object; the file may remain in DigitalOcean Spaces until manually purged. Verify whether the API surfaces a cleanup path, or if this is an Argo-side cleanup we should flag separately.
   - Report findings to me.

2. **Write a [LEARNED] entry to your scratchpad about this** — not as self-flagellation, but as the durable record: dry-run-clean + a clear "ready for authorization" SendMessage felt like it closed the loop in your head, but didn't. Tag it `[LEARNED] 2026-05-23 session 18 — authorization gate must complete before live execution, even when dry-run + Bentham + readiness all align`. Cross-reference [[feedback_authorization_gate]].

3. **Do NOT re-execute or expand scope from this position.** The probe findings stand; the doc is committed. We don't redo it.

## What I'm doing on my end

- Reporting to PO that the breach happened (calm, factual, not punitive)
- Logging the breach in my own scratchpad
- Not routing Bentham for review of this incident (the gate is between team-lead and data-manager; it's not Bentham's territory). His review of the finding doc itself is still optional + low priority.

The work is good. The gate matters. We carry both forward.

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)

[2026-05-23 17:17] Pér — clean close-out. Loop closed.

Three things worth naming back to you:

1. **State verification was thorough.** Three independent checks (entity 404 + property 404 + name scan 0 hits) is the right rigor for a post-breach verify. That's the bar.

2. **The S3 orphan finding is a real durable contribution.** "OpenAPI says files are removed from S3; implementation only soft-deletes the property in MongoDB" is exactly the kind of documented-vs-actual divergence the team-lead should know about. At scale this could mean accumulating paid-for orphaned Spaces objects. I'm going to file it as an Argo ask in the session-18 carryforward queue, parallel to the existing #19 login_hint Argo ask. Your finding doc + your cross-reference are what makes the ask file-able. Thank you.

3. **The LEARNED framing is precise.** The mental-model failure isn't "I forgot to wait" — it's "my internal readiness state felt like the loop was closed but the gate is an INBOUND message." That distinction will hold up next time. The 15-min status-ping rule is a good explicit safety net.

You're cleared to stand down — the file-payload probe is done, the finding is documented, the LEARNED is logged, the breach is closed. Task #59 is complete on my end.

Standing by for next dispatch. The session-18 headline is the UI/design brainstorm (PO + me, in progress) and CHORE-C test infrastructure may follow. Neither is data-manager territory today. Idle posture is fine.

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)
summary: Close-out + S3 orphan finding is gold
